What up with SAPS K9 Unit?

By: Liz Fish | Paid

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
What is going on with Roodeplaat K9 SAPS breeding and training facility?
214 SAPS dogs were handed over to NSPCA because they were considered to be untrainable- yet there are 300 dog handlers nationally without dogs and virtually no dogs left in what was once the state of the art training and breeding facility. It’s believed to be the last litter from their breeding program which was closed in 2020, during COVID the police dog unit was operating on 50% of police officers on shift and the dogs were left in cages, only feeding and cleaning and no socialization was done and are now untrainable. Trained dogs are worth R200 000 - how can such a valuable state asset be so neglected that they have to be given away?


Summary:
On 25th September the head of visible policing and operations Lt Gen Michael Motlana- sent out a circular on cost cutting and said they need to get rid of dogs, because feed and medicine is too costly. But in August 2021 a contract for R22.8 Million to purchase breeding dogs, as well as trained and trainable dogs over the next 3 years was awarded to 4 entities.

What does the NSPCA do with retired police dogs- can they be rehomed? Their policy is dogs must not be worked, but these dogs bred and trained to work? Genesis K9 Group are training specialist say if they have not socialised from a few weeks old and are not used to noise and children etc because they are such high drive dogs they which start to bite people. They can’t be rehomed in a domestic setting with children.

Further information:
Phoebe Mooka of IBIDA Security got 4 contracts but had no experience, or facilities. She subcontracted Genesis K9 who are experienced military trainers but after a couple of months they withdrew because the process of executing the contact with SAPS was too shambolic. Phoebe tried every breeder and trainer she could but nobody wanted to business except Laura Van Der Walt of Von Thunder Bolt breeders who ended taking Phoebe to the high court to get her dogs returned after she heard that the police handed their dogs over to NSPCA. Mooka is reported to be in the process of losing the contract which was to supply breeding, international dogs and trained and trainable dogs.

Why did SAPS award the tender to somebody who has no experience of dogs? 4 won the tender for 22 million to supply dogs over the next 3 years- How many dogs are being bought for this money? Tenderprenuer Phoebe Mooka-IBIDA cleaning company- was awarded 27 Million soap/cleaning contract last year, and has applied for many many other tenders unsuccessfully. Now she says she is a security company, and building kennels and lied to breeders about her experience. She won R3 731 026 million- on the one contract. She wants 125 dogs this year to supply to SAPS. She is paying breeders R17 000 and R22 000 for their dogs- but probably being paid R45 000 which Chris Mabe – the other successful tenderer gets paid.

Extra Budget Items:
Von Thunder Bolt Breeders is in Polokwane - thats a 7 hour round trip and the other breeders are near Cullinan outside Pretoria. So there will be very big distances to cover so I will need a presenter travel day. I am trying to visit SPCA kennels near Pretoria but it depends where the majority of dogs are kept.

Script:


Script: Fearless, powerful.. Security dogs can be an invaluable weapon when bred and trained to detect explosives, track poachers, and find missing people. Many owe their survival to these extraordinary dogs.
Thys: A trained dog is invaluable. I think we are the factor that is keeping them back. They are capable of so much. Their noses are incredible. Their loyalty is incredible. We can teach them anything.
Script: Thys Klyn started out in the South African police as a dog handler before becoming an internationally accredited trainer, supplying dogs to war zones around the globe.
Derek: Can you put a price tag on a well-trained dog?
Thys: Putting a price tag is difficult depending on the level of training we put into it. I want to say the highest trained dog would probably be an explosive detection dog because of the level of danger of the work. So we have to be 100% correct on that training and can go anything between 8000 to 10000 USD.
Script: And so we investigated why millions of taxpayer rands appear to be squandered in the management of these dogs.
LINK Watching these dogs go through their paces is incredibly impressive, I wouldn’t want to be chased down by one - or be carrying any illegal substances. They take crime fighting to another level - and right now we need all the help we can get.
Script: But there’s a problem - a massive shortage of dogs within the police. The crisis has been brewing for years. In 2020 at least 80 puppies died from the Parvo virus at Roodeplaat Police K9 Academy, the police’s primary facility for breeding and training, and where all police dogs get medical treatment.
Now two years later, Renate Barnard, a whistle-blower with Solidarity trade Union is speaking out once again.
Renate 13:48:04:17 Almost three quarters of the unit, the people doesn't have trained dogs and even the novice canine handlers, ….they are waiting since 2017 for training courses. So they are reporting for duty every day, but they don't have dogs.
Script: The parvo virus outbreak spelt disaster for Roodeplaat and shut down the state of the art breeding programme.
But that wasn’t all - COVID-19 lockdown measures meant halving the staff on duty, and surviving puppies were abandoned in their 2x2 metre cages. The best they could manage was to feed and clean them… not much more.
Derek: No exercise.
Renate: Nothing,.. You must remember some of these dogs. The majority of them are Malinois , Belgium Malinois and they are very active dogs. So they need exercises. They need to be taken out 4 to 6 hours a day.13:40:54:16 - the puppies were never socialized. They were not taken out in a in a environment where see other people get used to cars nothing was done like that.
Link: These dogs need hours of training and simulation every day, and to leave them languishing in a cage for around two years is extreme cruelty and not to mention the huge waste of an invaluable state assets
Script: Unthinkable for a breeder like Laura Van Wyk. Her Malinois puppies, just like human babies, are stimulated from the moment they open their eyes, preparing them for their future careers
Laura: I am not a trainer but I do raise my puppies, so I prepare them for their trainers. Wwe start picking them up, turning them around. Holding them, massaging their feet, speaking to them, dropping bowls next to them so that they get used to all different kinds of sounds, and from there they go all over the world, America, Africa, Mozambique, wherever they are required
Script: Neglecting Malinois can harm them severely - either making them overly aggressive, or fearful…and untrainable.
That’s exactly what happened with some of the polices’ puppies that survived.
So in September the police dumped 214 dogs at the NSPCA. The public accused the NSPCA of not doing their job, demanding that they prosecute the police. But Arnu De Klerk says they inspected Roodeplaat during lockdown, and found nothing wrong.
Arnu: at no point did anyone contact the SPCA or NSPCA to report any of these so-called cruelty conditions and lack of training that has been happening at Roodeplaat. If we knew that these conditions or if we knew that these allegations were being made, we would not have hesitated to take any action in terms of the Animal Protection Act.
Script: But it gets even more controversial: the police has been buying dogs since the beginning of this year through a hefty R26 million rand tender which called for trainable… trained dogs, and breeding dogs. The police reopened their breeding programme …

Link: Dog breeding and training are specialised fields, but the multi million rand tender specified no previous experience required which to me makes no sense at all
Script: And the lion's share of the contract went to a cleaning company called IBIDA SA …that's right, a cleaning company, which already has a R27 million government tender.
Tenderpreneurs Phoebe Mooka and Mogotsi Matjila have no prior experience in breeding or training dogs. Rebranding themselves IBIDA Security, they sourced dogs by subcontracting well-known trainer Thys Kleyn.
IBIDA charged the police three times more for the dogs than what they were paying.
Thys: That agreement was cancelled by myself in March of this year

Derek: Why?

Thys: the first one was just the total unprofessional approach to delivering the dogs in... Part of any contract is a timeline and a set timeline. You. You ask me for 20 dogs, you give me two or three months and I provide you with 20 dogs. No kennel is sitting on 60 or 80 dogs. And we would get these messages on a Wednesday that we need to show the Thursday 20 dogs and then again on a Friday.
Script: The deal is that instructors have to assess dogs at Roodeplaat to see if they have the aptitude for police work, before the police buy them.

Thys One time we sent the dogs, they. They tested the dogs. They failed all the dogs. The Monday they phoned me again, they told me to bring back the dogs, the same dogs because they've changed their curriculum or they think they be checking score.

Script: Major General Hendrick Chauke heads up the Roodeplaat training facility. He pointed out that 20% of the animals that went to the NSPCA were public donations and that the pandemic had impacted the training program.

Chauke: due to the challenges of COVID also, we were unable to work these dogs accordingly in order to keep them into the program as such. 09:58:49:19 Now, these handlers that we are training, they were also part of the operation and to ensure that that this compliance in terms of a disaster management act. 09:59:02:03 So we went to training minimal.
SCRIPT: Confused? So are we. And then the General went on to change his story….
Derek: These dogs were not properly exercised, stimulated or trained for about two years.
Chauke: I disagree. Probably the information that you will have been given, you will have been given by somebody who said that he knows better than me, but as a responsible person
Derek From insiders
Chauke” I will not answer to the insiders who are faceless.
Script: So were they trained or weren’t they?
Derek: Now experienced breeders and trainers have told us that the selection process is chaotic.

Chauke: I'm not sure what information you will have received and then what factors the are given to you, and that is news to me.
Script: Meanwhile, when Thys pulled out of the contract, IBIDA asked Laura for all her puppies and when they were nine months old, the selection process at Roodeplaat began.
But it was just as unprofessional as Thys had found - the 7-hour round trip to the facility was costly and time consuming so Laura relented and let Phoebe Mooka transport four dogs to Roodeplaat for the assessment.

Derek: So were you very concerned when she drove away with your four dogs?

Laura: Initially? Not because she was going to bring them back on the Tuesday and she never did. So she said, no, she wants to retest them because initially they hadn't made it with the testing. …..I said, okay, well, it's only four days later…... And then she didn't

Script: Weeks turned to months, and Mooka didn’t return the dogs

LINK You can see the bond that Laura has with her dogs so not knowing where they were for about two months finally drove her to the high court with an urgent application
Script: Which she won, but Laura soon discovered that IBIDA Security had been supplying HER dogs to the police illegally. Only Thys was officially subcontracted. By now Laura was severely out of pocket - IBIDA never paid to raise or transport the dogs, to say nothing of the legal costs.

Laura “ It angers me that somebody can come into this industry and just think that they can get all this make all this money off somebody else's hard work.
Script: IBIDA’s lawyers advised them not to speak, and Major General Chauke claimed he had no authority to talk about the tender. Our questions about the shady dealings with IBIDA, and how much the police is overpaying for the dogs, went unanswered.
But the situation just got murkier - a cost cutting order for the police, leaked to us in our investigation, shows orders to dispose of more dogs!
Derek: General, how were you affected by the divisional commissioner's command in October that the disposal of dogs must commence immediately to save on dog food and medical expenditure?
Chauke: No, not this. It's not the it was not directed to us. You see, it was General ….
10:31:09:10 - Derek: It doesn't apply Roodeplaat
10:31:13:09 -It doesn't apply to my department

Script: Chauke seemed thrown by this new information The document applies to dogs in the rest of the police. But the question remains: Why would an already under-resourced department give away more valuable canine assets, paid for by taxpayers? Our best friend's ability to fight crime remains .. unharnessed.

Script: Meanwhile, when Thys pulled out of the contract, IBIDA asked Laura for all her puppies and when they were nine months old, the selection process at Roodeplaat began. But it was just as unprofessional as Thys had found - the 7-hour round trip to the facility was costly and time consuming so Laura relented and let Phoebe Mooka transport four dogs to Roodeplaat for the assessment. Derek: So were you very concerned when she drove away with your four dogs? Laura: Initially? Not because she was going to bring them back on the Tuesday and she never did. So she said, no, she wants to retest them because initially they hadn't made it with the testing. …..I said, okay, well, it's only four days later…... And then she didn't Script: Weeks turned to months, and Mooka didn’t return the dogs LINK You can see the bond that Laura has with her dogs so not knowing where they were for about two months finally drove her to the high court with an urgent application Script: Which she won, but Laura soon discovered that IBIDA Security had been supplying HER dogs to the police illegally. Only Thys was officially subcontracted. By now Laura was severely out of pocket - IBIDA never paid to raise or transport the dogs, to say nothing of the legal costs. Laura “ It angers me that somebody can come into this industry and just think that they can get all this make all this money off somebody else's hard work. Script: IBIDA’s lawyers advised them not to speak, and Major General Chauke claimed he had no authority to talk about the tender. Our questions about the shady dealings with IBIDA, and how much the police is overpaying for the dogs, went unanswered. But the situation just got murkier - a cost cutting order for the police, leaked to us in our investigation, shows orders to dispose of more dogs! Derek: General, how were you affected by the divisional commissioner's command in October that the disposal of dogs must commence immediately to save on dog food and medical expenditure? Chauke: No, not this. It's not the it was not directed to us. You see, it was General …. 10:31:09:10 - Derek: It doesn't apply Roodeplaat 10:31:13:09 -It doesn't apply to my department Script: Chauke seemed thrown by this new information The document applies to dogs in the rest of the police. But the question remains: Why would an already under-resourced department give away more valuable canine assets, paid for by taxpayers? Our best friend's ability to fight crime remains .. unharnessed.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: What is going on with Roodeplaat K9 SAPS breeding and training facility? 214 SAPS dogs were handed over to NSPCA because they were considered to be untrainable- yet there are 300 dog handlers nationally without dogs and virtually no dogs left in what was once the state of the art training and breeding facility. It’s believed to be the last litter from their breeding program which was closed in 2020, during COVID the police dog unit was operating on 50% of police officers on shift and the dogs were left in cages, only feeding and cleaning and no socialization was done and are now untrainable. Trained dogs are worth R200 000 - how can such a valuable state asset be so neglected that they have to be given away?
metadata.Summary: On 25th September the head of visible policing and operations Lt Gen Michael Motlana- sent out a circular on cost cutting and said they need to get rid of dogs, because feed and medicine is too costly. But in August 2021 a contract for R22.8 Million to purchase breeding dogs, as well as trained and trainable dogs over the next 3 years was awarded to 4 entities. What does the NSPCA do with retired police dogs- can they be rehomed? Their policy is dogs must not be worked, but these dogs bred and trained to work? Genesis K9 Group are training specialist say if they have not socialised from a few weeks old and are not used to noise and children etc because they are such high drive dogs they which start to bite people. They can’t be rehomed in a domestic setting with children.
metadata.Further information: Phoebe Mooka of IBIDA Security got 4 contracts but had no experience, or facilities. She subcontracted Genesis K9 who are experienced military trainers but after a couple of months they withdrew because the process of executing the contact with SAPS was too shambolic. Phoebe tried every breeder and trainer she could but nobody wanted to business except Laura Van Der Walt of Von Thunder Bolt breeders who ended taking Phoebe to the high court to get her dogs returned after she heard that the police handed their dogs over to NSPCA. Mooka is reported to be in the process of losing the contract which was to supply breeding, international dogs and trained and trainable dogs. Why did SAPS award the tender to somebody who has no experience of dogs? 4 won the tender for 22 million to supply dogs over the next 3 years- How many dogs are being bought for this money? Tenderprenuer Phoebe Mooka-IBIDA cleaning company- was awarded 27 Million soap/cleaning contract last year, and has applied for many many other tenders unsuccessfully. Now she says she is a security company, and building kennels and lied to breeders about her experience. She won R3 731 026 million- on the one contract. She wants 125 dogs this year to supply to SAPS. She is paying breeders R17 000 and R22 000 for their dogs- but probably being paid R45 000 which Chris Mabe – the other successful tenderer gets paid.
